summary: Backend-only retest of Ponto 5 (per-(company, phone, connection) ticket uniqueness) after the LID fallback fix. Created /app/backend/tests/test_iteration_67.py (9 tests) covering webhook per-connection isolation, from_me paused ticket, LID fallback both branches, group ticket keying, and the connection-aware duplicate guard on POST /api/crm/tickets. All 9 pass. Regression suites (test_manual_message_dedup_and_transfer, test_bot_pause_api, test_flow_engine_ticket_menu, test_iteration_66 = 28 tests) all pass. No blocking defects found; 2 consistency gaps flagged for review.

minor.issue: Open-ticket lookup is NOT connection-scoped (matches by client_id/phone only). With Ponto 5 semantics, an operator working on connection B who opens a chat for a client that already has an open ticket on connection A will be dropped into A's ticket, mixing history — inconsistent with the webhook and POST /tickets behaviour.

Comment says 'Find an OPEN ticket for this number (same connection)' but the query has no connection_id filter; the gateway message can be appended to a ticket owned by a different connection while outbound is sent via gw['connection_id'] → mismatch between ticket owner and sending instance.

By-design trade-off, verified empirically: the $or clause lets ANY open ticket in the tenant that has no connection_id and an outgoing in the last 5 min absorb an @lid inbound arriving on ANY connection. Reproduced (a manual no-connection ticket stole a LID inbound sent on a different connection). Acceptable for backward-compat but worth narrowing (e.g. also require matching push_name, or stamp connection_id on manual tickets at creation).

action_items: Decide/align connection scoping for POST /api/crm/tickets/open-or-create (crm_routes ~398) — currently cross-connection.
Add connection_id filter to the SGP gateway open-ticket lookup (sgp_gateway_routes ~362) to match its own comment.
Optional: tighten LID fallback strategy 1 (no-connection tickets are matched tenant-wide).
critical_code_review_comments: channels_routes.py is 2293 lines — webhook_message alone spans ~300 lines; split webhook handling into a dedicated module for maintainability.

Verified duplicate-guard ordering in POST /api/crm/tickets: the 409 check runs BEFORE _ensure_user_can_use_connection, so a duplicate on a disconnected connection returns 409 (not 400). Consistent and intentional, but note in API docs.
Ticket responses correctly exclude Mongo _id (asserted in test).
seed_data_creation: 3 connected WhatsApp connections (TEST_it67_conn_A/B/C) inserted directly into channel_connections for the crmtest tenant, plus webhook/CRM-created tickets and clients. All TEST_it67_* records deleted in module teardown — verified 0 leftovers in tickets/channel_connections/clients/message_log.

context_for_next_testing_agent: test_iteration_67.py is self-cleaning and re-runnable. Note: the LID strategy-1 branch matches ANY tenant ticket without connection_id having a recent last_outgoing_at, so tests that seed such tickets must delete them before testing cross-connection isolation (already handled inside the file). Webhook payload keys: instance_id, phone, name, message, message_id, from_me, timestamp, is_group, group_jid, group_subject, lid_jid, is_lid.
rca_of_the_issue: No product defect reproduced this iteration. Initial test failure was self-inflicted contamination: the previous test's manual (no connection_id) ticket with a recent outgoing absorbed the LID inbound via the intentionally broad $or clause — which itself confirms the documented backward-compat trade-off of the fix.
